layoutNotes:
DIR + EXPORT STRATEGY: aws-autoscaling ports into a NEW subdirectory src/aws/compute/auto-scaling/ (kebab dir) exported from src/aws/compute/index.ts as a jsii submodule via `export * as autoscaling from "./auto-scaling";` — NOT flattened. This is mandated by the established compute/index.ts pattern (`export * as autoscalingcommon from "./autoscaling-common"`, `export * as tasks`, `export * as lbtargets`, `export * as alpha`, `export * as sources`, `export * as destinations`; notify uses `export * as targets`) and is the only jsii-safe way to avoid flat-barrel class-name collisions.

COLLISIONS (why flattening is impossible): compute/ ALREADY flattens the aws-applicationautoscaling twins at the root (index.ts lines 111-116: base-scalable-attribute, schedule, scalable-target, step-scaling-policy, step-scaling-action, target-tracking-scaling-policy). aws-autoscaling re-declares colliding names: Schedule + CronOptions (vs appscaling schedule.ts), StepScalingAction + AdjustmentType + MetricAggregationType (vs appscaling step-scaling-action.ts), StepScalingPolicy + BasicStepScalingPolicyProps + StepScalingPolicyProps + ScalingInterval (vs appscaling step-scaling-policy.ts), TargetTrackingScalingPolicy + BaseTargetTrackingProps + PredefinedMetric (vs appscaling target-tracking-scaling-policy.ts). Namespacing under `autoscaling.*` resolves ALL of them with zero flat-barrel collisions. Consumers reach the big construct as compute.autoscaling.AutoScalingGroup.

RELATION TO appscaling files (MUST NOT DUPLICATE): the appscaling twins are the closest structural exemplars and each aws-autoscaling file should mirror its twin's terraconstructs shape, BUT they are genuinely different classes (appscaling targets IScalableTarget + appautoscalingPolicy resource + ServiceNamespace; aws-autoscaling targets IAutoScalingGroup + autoscalingPolicy resource). The one truly shared, already-ported dependency is aws-autoscaling-common: it lives at src/aws/compute/autoscaling-common/ (interval-utils findAlarmThresholds/normalizeIntervals, types, test-utils) — step-scaling-policy.ts imports it via `../autoscaling-common/interval-utils`; DO NOT re-port it. Schedule/StepScaling/TargetTracking are ported fresh INSIDE the auto-scaling namespace, not reused from the flat appscaling files.

VOLUME (critical): upstream aws-autoscaling/lib/volume.ts is a duplicate of the EC2 block-device types and MUST NOT be ported. src/aws/compute/volume.ts (the EC2 Volume port) already exports the identical set (BlockDevice, EbsDeviceOptionsBase, EbsDeviceOptions, EbsDeviceSnapshotOptions, EbsDeviceProps, BlockDeviceVolume, EbsDeviceVolumeType). auto-scaling-group.ts imports them from ../volume, and auto-scaling/index.ts RE-EXPORTS them so the namespace API keeps autoscaling.BlockDeviceVolume / autoscaling.EbsDeviceVolumeType (used by the upstream asg-lt integ and by ASG blockDevices prop).

PROVIDER RESOURCE MAPPING: CfnAutoScalingGroup->autoscalingGroup.AutoscalingGroup, CfnLifecycleHook->autoscalingLifecycleHook.AutoscalingLifecycleHook, CfnScheduledAction->autoscalingSchedule.AutoscalingSchedule, CfnScalingPolicy->autoscalingPolicy.AutoscalingPolicy (NOT appautoscalingPolicy — the appscaling twins use appautoscalingPolicy; do not copy that import blindly), CfnWarmPool->inline warm_pool block on aws_autoscaling_group (no standalone resource — WarmPool mutates the parent ASG), CfnLaunchConfiguration->prefer launchTemplate.LaunchTemplate (the launch-template branch is the default emit path; launch-configuration is legacy/no-op).

ORDERING & CYCLES: IAutoScalingGroup (defined in the order-4 hub auto-scaling-group.ts) is a pervasive FORWARD type-reference for the order-2/3 children — import it as a type; the converter reads the upstream interface to know its shape. Two genuine cycles exist: (a) lifecycle-hook.ts <-> lifecycle-hook-target.ts (type-only, safe, ordered target@2 then hook@3); (b) auto-scaling-group.ts <-> aspects/require-imdsv2-aspect.ts (RUNTIME cycle: hub@4 imports the aspect class, aspect@5 imports the AutoScalingGroup class — resolved because usage is at call time; convert hub first with a forward import, aspect after). Files sharing an order number never import each other. Order: 1=[termination-policy, schedule]; 2=[step-scaling-action, target-tracking-scaling-policy, scheduled-action, warm-pool, lifecycle-hook-target]; 3=[step-scaling-policy, lifecycle-hook]; 4=[auto-scaling-group]; 5=[aspects/require-imdsv2-aspect]; 6=[aspects/index, index].
